info.desc: Stadium Arcadium is the ninth studio album by alternative rock band Red Hot Chili Peppers, released on May 9, 2006 via Warner Bros. Records. It sold 442,000 copies in the U.S. in the first week and debuted at number one on the Billboard 200. The album spawned five hit singles: "Dani California", "Snow ((Hey Oh))", "Desecration Smile", "Hump De Bump", and "Tell Me Baby". According to the band's frontman Anthony Kiedis, Stadium Arcadium was originally scheduled to be a trilogy of albums each released six months apart, but was eventually condensed into a double album. Stadium Arcadium was critically praised .

podcast.body: This album marked the end of John Frusciante's second tenure with the Red Hot Chili Peppers. While it may not be universally considered the band's absolute best, Frusciante's guitar work on "Stadium Arcadium" is widely regarded as fantastic and a tribute to guitar classics like Jimi Hendrix. Several guitar and rock music publications recognize this work as among the best in his entire career, holding it in high esteem despite its potentially less famous status. "el trabajo de guitarra que hizo, fuse ante en el estadio Arquedium es fantástico, es casi un tributo a los grandes clásicos de la guitarra como Jimmy Hendrix."

It spawned the hit single "Dani California" and went on to sell approximately 6.5 million copies by the end of the decade, making it one of the few commercial bright spots for the recording industry during a dismal period of declining sales. "The Red Hot Chili Peppers with Danny California, a single from their double disc Stadium Arcadia, which came out on May 5, 2006, and eventually sold about 6.5 million copies by the end of the decade."

podcast.body: This massive double album, originally intended to be a triple album, was released on May 9, 2006, and showcased John Frusciante's new approaches to improvised solos, funky rhythms, and melodic lessons. It sold millions, became the first Chili Peppers album to reach number one on the American album charts, and won five out of seven Grammy nominations. "Stadium Arcadium came out on May 9 2006 and it sold in the millions. It was the first Chili Peppers album to reach number one on the American album charts and it was nominated for seven Grammys and it won five."
